claim: A measurement-theory critique argues LLM judges have weak construct validity: even SOTA judges show best-in-class accuracy below 0.7 on alignment datasets, conflate distinct dimensions like fluency and relevance, and follow their own interpretations rather than the rubric.
quote: LLMs frequently rely on their own interpretations of evaluation criteria, rather than following the instructions provided in the prompts ... conflate distinct dimensions of evaluation, such as fluency and relevance

claim: LLM safety judges are brittle and gameable: small output modifications can cause them to misclassify up to 100% of harmful generations as harmless, and they rely on surface-level statistical cues rather than substantive reasoning.
quote: small modifications in outputs can lead LLMs safety judges to misclassify up to 100% of harmful generation as harmless

claim: On the 2025 USA Math Olympiad, every model except Gemini-2.5-Pro (25%) scored under 5% on rigorous proof generation, exposing that answer-only benchmarks vastly overstate reasoning competence.
quote: only Gemini-2.5-Pro achieves a non-trivial score of 25%, while all other models achieve less than 5%

claim: LLM judges systematically overgrade flawed math proofs: in proof-verification studies GPT-5 judged 7 of 48 candidates as correct despite all containing critical mathematical errors, showing >90% claimed accuracy does not yield reliable judgment on hard problems.
quote: GPT-5 judged 7 out of 48 candidates as correct, despite all of them having critical mathematical errors

claim: Cohere's Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) uses three smaller models from disjoint families (Command R, Haiku, GPT-3.5) with voting; it outperforms a single large GPT-4 judge, exhibits less intra-model bias, and is over seven times cheaper.
quote: Using a PoLL composed of a larger number of smaller models outperforms a single large judge, exhibits less intra-model bias due to its composition of disjoint model families, and does so while being over seven times less expensive

claim: Prometheus 2 is an open evaluator (Mistral-7B and 8x7B) trained on synthetic GPT-4 data handling both direct assessment and pairwise ranking with user-defined rubrics, closely mirroring human and GPT-4 judgements.
quote: Prometheus 2 ... closely mirrors human and GPT-4 judgements and is capable of processing both direct assessment and pair-wise ranking formats grouped with user-defined evaluation criteria

claim: Meta's Self-Taught Evaluator forgoes human preference labels: iterative DPO on synthetic contrasting outputs lifts a Llama3-70B judge from 75.4% to 88.3% on RewardBench (88.7% with majority voting), matching reward models trained on human annotations.
quote: the model based on Llama3-70B-Instruct sees its performance increase from 75.4% to 88.3% (or 88.7% with majority voting), matching ... top reward models trained on human annotations

claim: Atla Selene Mini is an open 8B judge that outperforms GPT-4o-mini and rival small judge models (SFR-Judge, Glider, Flow Judge, Prometheus 2), ranking best small-LM-judge across 11 benchmarks for absolute scoring, classification, and pairwise tasks.
quote: Selene Mini is the best SLMJ overall across 11 benchmarks spanning absolute scoring, classification, and pairwise evaluation tasks

claim: JudgeLM, an open fine-tuned LLM judge for open-ended answers, was accepted as an ICLR 2025 Spotlight; its repo has ~435 GitHub stars.
quote: [ICLR 2025 Spotlight] An open-sourced LLM judge for evaluating LLM-generated answers.

claim: The prometheus-eval toolkit (training/serving/using Prometheus judge models) has ~1,091 GitHub stars; the original prometheus repo has ~320.
quote: Evaluate your LLM's response with Prometheus and GPT4
